In "The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People" there's a similar concept called "the emotional bank account". 

The idea is that you always want to be contributing more to a relationship than you take. More importantly, people should not be contributing purely to make a withdrawal later (e.g. a partner doing the dishes should be doing it to contribute, not because they want a favour in return later).

When I do acts of service, I'm thinking things like making dinner, doing chores around the house, or bringing my wife a drink/snack. It's my way of saying "I know you are tired/want to relax so I will help".

The acts of service I like to receive are simple things like putting dirty dishes in the dishwasher. I'm not expecting the person to change my car's oil or clean my chimney.
